--- title: "[Binomial]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Binomial family with logit (canonical) link. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-psis-loo/whittaker/families/binomial.py#L14-L276){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python Binomial() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The Binomial family models a response that is either binary (`0`/`1`) or a proportion in `[0, 1]` (e.g. the fraction of successes out of a known number of trials). The logit link maps the unit interval to the whole real line, so the linear predictor is unconstrained while the fitted mean is always a valid probability. Use it for classification-style GAMs, for aggregated success/trial proportions, or wherever the outcome represents the probability of an event. The logit link additionally gives coefficients a log-odds interpretation: a one-unit increase in a covariate changes the log-odds of success by `coefficient`, and multiplies the odds by `exp(coefficient)`. ::: ## Notes {.doc-notes} The canonical link is the logit function: $$ g(\mu) = \log\!\left(\frac{\mu}{1-\mu}\right) $$ with inverse the logistic sigmoid $\mu = g^{-1}(\eta) = 1 / (1 + e^{-\eta})$. The variance function is $$ V(\mu) = \mu(1-\mu), $$ which is largest near $\mu = 0.5$ and shrinks toward zero as $\mu$ approaches either boundary. The deviance is $$ D(y, \hat\mu) = 2 \sum_i \left[ y_i \log\!\left(\frac{y_i}{\hat\mu_i}\right) + (1 - y_i) \log\!\left(\frac{1 - y_i}{1 - \hat\mu_i}\right) \right] . $$ ## Examples {.doc-examples} Fit a GAM to a binary outcome with a smooth, nonlinear log-odds relationship: ::: {#8604161e .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import whittaker as wk from scipy.special import expit rng = np.random.default_rng(0) n = 300 x = np.linspace(-3, 3, n) p = expit(np.sin(x)) y = rng.binomial(1, p) data = {"x": x, "y": y} model = wk.GAM("y ~ s(x)", family=wk.Binomial()) model.fit(data, method="REML") print(model.summary()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` GAM fit summary ============================================================ Formula: y ~ s(x) Family: Binomial(link='logit') Inference: REML Observations: 300 Coefficients: 10 Parametric coefficients: Term Estimate Std.Err z value p-value ------------------------ ---------- ---------- ---------- ---------- (Intercept) -0.0002 0.1170 -0.002 0.9984 Approximate significance of smooth terms: Term EDF Ref.df Chi.sq p-value ------------------------ ------ ------ ---------- ---------- s(x) 2.79 3 9.389 0.02454 Total EDF: 3.79 Scale est: 1.000000 Deviance: 404.3107 Null dev: 415.8883 Dev. expl: 2.8% GCV score: 1.382449 AIC: 411.90 BIC: 425.95 ``` ::: ::: ## Attributes {.doc-attributes}
Name Description
scale_known Whether the dispersion parameter is fixed. Always `True` for Binomial.
### [scale_known]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Whether the dispersion parameter is fixed. Always `True` for Binomial. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [scale_known]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} The Bernoulli/Binomial distribution has no free dispersion parameter, so the scale is fixed at `1` and is never estimated during fitting. This affects how `GAM.summary()` reports the scale and how many degrees of freedom are attributed to dispersion. ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods}
Name Description
deviance() Total binomial deviance, the (weighted) sum of `unit_deviance`.
initialize() Starting values for `mu`: a constant shrunk toward the overall mean of `y`.
link() Apply the logit link: $\eta = \log(\mu / (1-\mu))$.
link_derivative() Derivative of the logit link: $g'(\mu) = 1 / (\mu(1-\mu))$.
link_inverse() Apply the inverse logit link (logistic sigmoid): $\mu = 1 / (1 + e^{-\eta})$.
log_likelihood() Bernoulli/binomial log-likelihood $\ell_i = y_i \log(\mu_i) + (1-y_i)\log(1-\mu_i)$.
simulate() Simulate Bernoulli response values with success probability `mu`.
unit_deviance() Per-observation binomial deviance contributions.
variance() Binomial variance function: $V(\mu) = \mu(1-\mu)$.
### [deviance()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Total binomial deviance, the (weighted) sum of `unit_deviance`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-psis-loo/whittaker/families/binomial.py#L137-L157){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python deviance(y, mu, *, weights=None) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values (0/1 or proportions in `[0, 1]`), shape `(n,)`. [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Fitted conditional mean values (probabilities), shape `(n,)`. [weights]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional prior weights, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The total (weighted) deviance. ::: ### [initialize()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Starting values for `mu`: a constant shrunk toward the overall mean of `y`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-psis-loo/whittaker/families/binomial.py#L256-L273){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python initialize(y) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Every observation is initialized to `(mean(y) + 0.5) / 2`, a value strictly inside `(0, 1)` regardless of whether `y` contains only `0`s, only `1`s, or a mix, avoiding `logit(0)` or `logit(1)` on the first P-IRLS iteration. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Starting values for `mu`, shape `(n,)`. ::: ### [link()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Apply the logit link: $\eta = \log(\mu / (1-\mu))$. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-psis-loo/whittaker/families/binomial.py#L72-L85){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python link(mu) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Conditional mean values (probabilities), shape `(n,)`. Must lie in `(0, 1)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Linear predictor (log-odds) values, shape `(n,)`. ::: ### [link_derivative()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Derivative of the logit link: $g'(\mu) = 1 / (\mu(1-\mu))$. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-psis-loo/whittaker/families/binomial.py#L102-L117){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python link_derivative(mu) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Conditional mean values (probabilities), shape `(n,)`; clipped away from `0` and `1` to avoid division by zero. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Derivative values, shape `(n,)`. ::: ### [link_inverse()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Apply the inverse logit link (logistic sigmoid): $\mu = 1 / (1 + e^{-\eta})$. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-psis-loo/whittaker/families/binomial.py#L87-L100){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python link_inverse(eta) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [eta]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Linear predictor (log-odds) values, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Conditional mean values (probabilities), shape `(n,)`, always in `(0, 1)`. ::: ### [log_likelihood()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Bernoulli/binomial log-likelihood $\ell_i = y_i \log(\mu_i) + (1-y_i)\log(1-\mu_i)$. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-psis-loo/whittaker/families/binomial.py#L187-L215){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python log_likelihood(y, mu, scale, *, weights=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The `scale` argument is accepted for interface compatibility but ignored, since the Binomial distribution has no free dispersion parameter (`scale_known` is `True`). ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values, shape `(n,)`. [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Fitted conditional mean values (probabilities), shape `(n,)`. [scale]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Ignored. [weights]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional prior weights, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The total log-likelihood. ::: ### [simulate()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Simulate Bernoulli response values with success probability `mu`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-psis-loo/whittaker/families/binomial.py#L236-L254){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python simulate(mu, scale, rng) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Success probabilities (fitted values), shape `(n,)`. [scale]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Ignored (the Binomial distribution has no free dispersion parameter). [rng]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [np.random.Generator]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A `numpy.random.Generator` instance. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Simulated 0/1 response values, shape `(n,)`. ::: ### [unit_deviance()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Per-observation binomial deviance contributions. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-psis-loo/whittaker/families/binomial.py#L159-L185){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python unit_deviance(y, mu) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Computes $d_i = 2 \left[ y_i \log(y_i/\hat\mu_i) + (1-y_i)\log((1-y_i)/(1-\hat\mu_i)) \right]$, with the usual conventions that the $y_i \log(\cdot)$ term vanishes when $y_i = 0$ and the $(1-y_i)\log(\cdot)$ term vanishes when $y_i = 1$. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values, shape `(n,)`. [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Fitted conditional mean values (probabilities), shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Per-observation deviance contributions, shape `(n,)`. ::: ### [variance()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Binomial variance function: $V(\mu) = \mu(1-\mu)$. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-psis-loo/whittaker/families/binomial.py#L119-L135){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python variance(mu) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Largest at $\mu = 0.5$ and shrinking toward zero as $\mu$ approaches either boundary. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Conditional mean values (probabilities), shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Variance values $\mu(1-\mu)$, shape `(n,)`. :::
